channel.title: DevPulse · Cloud & infra
channel.description: Daily cloud & infra stories worth an engineer's time.

item.title: RFC 8950 carries IPv4 routes over IPv6 next hops without tunnels
item.description: The setup lets IPv6-only network cores exchange IPv4 routes over IPv6 BGP sessions, leaving IPv4 at network edges without tunnels. It offers a practical path to reduce IPv4 configuration across backbones and IXPs.

item.title: Temporal Cloud scales pull-based workers on Cloud Run worker pools
item.description: In preview, Temporal Cloud can size Cloud Run worker pools to queued work, addressing the always-on cost and delayed autoscaling of polling workers. This is a useful pattern for operating queue-driven workloads, including agent workflows, on serverless infrastructure.

item.title: RPKI now protects 70% of internet routes, up from 54%
item.description: The report says RPKI coverage rose from 54% to 70% in a year and explains how route-origin validation addresses mistaken or malicious BGP announcements. Engineers operating networked services should understand this evolving layer of internet routing security.

item.title: BIPM moves to stop adding leap seconds to UTC
item.description: A 2026 resolution addresses the technical steps needed to preserve UTC continuity, including increasing the allowed difference between UTC and Earth-rotation time. Changes to the time standard can affect systems that depend on precise timestamps.

item.title: Flipflop creates persistent Iroh tunnels for file sharing
item.description: Flipflop connects devices over Bluetooth, LAN or the internet so they can exchange files and other content later. Its cross-network, persistent sharing model may interest engineers building peer-to-peer infrastructure.

item.title: Void combines Vite app development with Cloudflare deployment
item.description: Void open-sources a platform, SDK, and CLI for server routing, typed data access, resource provisioning, and deployment through a Vite workflow. Teams building full-stack apps can assess whether this integrated path simplifies their Cloudflare setup.

item.title: Repeated cable cuts expose submarine-network resilience risks
item.description: The Matsu Islands’ submarine cables were cut 27 times from 2018 to 2022, followed by four major outages from 2023 to 2025. The account points to the physical vulnerabilities and resilience challenges behind critical network links.

item.title: Headlamp traces Kueue admission decisions for suspended Kubernetes Jobs
item.description: The Kueue plugin for Headlamp lets operators follow a Workload through its condition and related queue, flavor, and cohort resources to diagnose admission delays. This is a practical troubleshooting path for Kubernetes resource scheduling.

item.title: Yandex traffic analysis finds malicious automation moved to other providers
item.description: Traffic analysis found Yandex Search’s drop came mostly from verified crawlers, while malicious activity shifted to other hosting providers. It shows why traffic declines at one provider do not necessarily mean automated abuse has stopped.

item.title: Lix 2.96 adds security and debugger work while advancing RPC and Rust support
item.description: Lix 2.96 focuses on security, debugger support, and quality-of-life improvements while continuing work on a Cap'n Proto RPC protocol and Rust support. The update is relevant to engineers maintaining Nix-based build and development infrastructure.

item.title: AWS Lambda Web Functions run standard HTTP servers without event-handler rewrites
item.description: AWS says Lambda Web Functions can run port-listening Node.js applications with a single command, while Lambda handles scaling, multi-region distribution and active CPU billing. The HTTP-native model could simplify deployment choices for teams weighing serverless against managed services.

item.title: NVIDIA open-sources Run:ai’s GPU scheduling and workload management components
item.description: The release splits the platform into four independently adoptable components for GPU-aware scheduling, GPU sharing, resource management, and workload management. This gives AI infrastructure teams more options for integrating GPU orchestration into their stacks.

item.title: jinx compiles Nix to TypeScript and matches nixpkgs derivation paths
item.description: The author says jinx evaluates all 231,777 nixpkgs attributes to the same derivation paths as Nix and can run in a browser without Nix installed. This is a concrete approach to making Nix's build model accessible through different tooling.

item.title: Meta announces liquid-cooled racks, 102.4T switches, and an AI transport protocol
item.description: Meta is sharing IcePack liquid-cooled network racks, an IceCube 102.4T switch platform, a GPU scale-out fabric, and the MetaRoCE transport protocol. These infrastructure changes matter to engineers building large AI clusters.

item.title: IRCv3 defines backward-compatible extensions to the IRC protocol
item.description: IRCv3’s working group develops protocol extensions designed to remain compatible with older clients and servers, alongside a roadmap and specifications. The protocol work is useful context for engineers building interoperable messaging systems.

item.title: HashiCorp ends Boundary Community Edition maintenance and security updates
item.description: Boundary CE is archived, with no future releases, bug fixes or security patches planned; existing binaries remain available. Teams relying on self-managed access control should reassess their support and security plans.

item.title: Texas pauses data center permits as grid requests reach 474 GW
item.description: The excerpt says Texas’s queue for large new grid customers grew from 63 GW at the end of 2024 to 474 GW by June, about 90% of it data centers, before a permitting freeze. The account examines power and interconnection constraints on large-scale compute.

item.title: Leaky buckets provide a clock-like model for software admission control
item.description: The piece connects leaky-bucket admission control to water clocks, where a steady outflow measures time and regulates when work can proceed. The model gives engineers a useful way to reason about gating actions when resources or priorities are constrained.

item.title: Deno team joins Cloudflare to pursue integrated application infrastructure
item.description: Deno says its work on Deno Deploy clarified an ambition to bring compute, storage and communication together rather than have every application assemble its own infrastructure. Engineers following runtimes and deployment platforms may want to watch how the teams pursue that model.

item.title: Carrier-Explode decodes and compares carrier settings across phones
item.description: The tool decodes iPhone, Pixel and Galaxy carrier settings, including APNs, VoLTE, Wi-Fi Calling and 5G, and exposes the data through an API and daily dataset. It could help engineers inspect how carrier configurations differ across devices.

item.title: Parseable displays OpenTelemetry traces from Datasette
item.description: The setup runs Parseable and sends it OpenTelemetry traces from Datasette, with Codex helping work out the integration. This is a practical example of wiring application traces into an observability platform.

item.title: 11 of 23 core open-source projects rely on one or two regular contributors
item.description: An analysis of 23 infrastructure projects counted contributors with at least ten changes in the past year and found that 11 had only one or two. The concentration highlights maintenance risk in dependencies that phones, browsers and servers rely on.

item.title: Design products to export telemetry to any OpenTelemetry backend
item.description: The guidance advocates exporting logs, traces and metrics through OpenTelemetry Protocol so customers can choose their observability backend. Engineers building SaaS or self-hosted products can use the approach to avoid locking telemetry into a vendor-specific stack.

item.title: SageMaker Studio can now manage HyperPod Spaces from its UI
item.description: Teams can launch JupyterLab and Code Editor environments on HyperPod EKS clusters from Studio without using command-line tools. This streamlines access to infrastructure for ML development, though the excerpt gives few implementation details.

item.title: Let’s Encrypt plans 64-day certificates starting in February 2027
item.description: Let’s Encrypt plans to issue 64-day certificates from February 10, 2027, then move to 45-day lifetimes in 2028. Operators will need to ensure certificate renewal and deployment workflows can handle shorter validity periods.

item.title: A runaway Durable Object alarm triggered a $10,811 Cloudflare bill
item.description: An alarm repeatedly rescheduled itself, producing 6 trillion reads and writes; Cloudflare did not refund the $10,811.41 bill, and the author says they will move projects to self-hosted VPSs. The failure shows how an unbounded serverless loop can turn into a large, uncapped cost.

item.title: Let’s Encrypt will default to 64-day certificates in February 2027
item.description: Let’s Encrypt plans to switch subscribers to 64-day certificates on February 10, 2027, and recommends testing renewals in staging and renewing around two-thirds of the certificate lifetime. Operators with date-based renewal logic should update it before the transition.

item.title: K10s adds mouse-driven navigation and cluster-wide search to a Kubernetes TUI
item.description: K10s combines clickable cluster actions with a single search for resource kinds and objects, and says startup registers no watches. Its interaction model and startup choices are useful details for engineers building operational tooling.

item.title: AWS reports Prime Day peaks of 2.3 trillion Lambda invocations per day
item.description: AWS says Lambda handled over 2.3 trillion invocations per day, EBS peaked at 24.8 trillion I/O operations, and Graviton powered up to 49% of EC2 compute used by Amazon.com. These production figures offer useful scale context for capacity and infrastructure planning.

item.title: One maintainer keeps the time zone database used across billions of phones current
item.description: The time zone database supplies clock rules to Android and iPhones, and Paul Eggert has coordinated updates since 2012; a recent release accounts for Manitoba’s move to permanent UTC−05. The story highlights the maintenance burden behind widely shared infrastructure.

item.title: Kubernetes is moving away from cgroup v1 toward v2
item.description: Kubernetes moved cgroup v1 management into maintenance in v1.31, and v1.35 defaults to refusing startup on cgroup v1 nodes unless overridden. Teams should plan node migration before upgrading.

item.title: Google Cloud’s U4 machines bring hardware-level networking to low-latency trading
item.description: Google Cloud’s ULL solution combines hardware-based multicast with network traffic capture timed at hardware level. Deterministic networking and replayable traffic are useful patterns for latency-sensitive distributed systems.

item.title: Perseus found 304 fail-slow cases across 248,000 drives and cut tail latency by 48%
item.description: Perseus uses a regression-based detector to identify drive-level fail-slow behavior; isolating detected drives reduced node-level 99.99th-percentile tail latency by 48%. The authors also released a production-derived dataset for studying storage degradation.

item.title: SageMaker HyperPod governance spans organization, project, cluster and workload controls
item.description: The guide covers identity, capacity and observability policies for shared HyperPod clusters, including access through SageMaker Unified Studio. These controls matter when multiple ML teams compete for accelerated compute.

item.title: DNSSEC resolvers must trust KSK-2024 before the 2026 root key rollover
item.description: Cloudflare says validating resolvers need to trust KSK-2024 ahead of the October 11, 2026 rollover, and notes that upgrades or machine moves previously caused resolvers to lose learned trust. Resolver operators should verify trust anchors before the switch.

item.title: Meta’s NTS time service authenticates packets without per-client server state
item.description: Meta’s public time service uses NTS, with stateless servers and cookie keys derived rather than stored or replicated; the implementation is open source. The design is a useful example of adding authenticated time while limiting server-side state.

item.title: PyTorch’s accelerator group advances vendor-neutral hardware integration
item.description: The working group is standardizing integration mechanisms and unified testing for diverse accelerators, with reference backends across PyTorch. These efforts affect how teams bring new compute platforms into AI software stacks.

item.title: AICR 1.0 stabilizes GPU cluster configuration interfaces and validation
item.description: AICR 1.0 sets stable contracts for its CLI, API, SDK and artifact schemas, with capabilities for snapshots, recipes, bundles and validation. Operators can use it to standardize GPU Kubernetes deployments and verify clusters against desired configurations.

item.title: GitHub Actions incident delayed or failed many hosted-runner jobs
item.description: During the incident’s peak, 47% of hosted-runner workflows failed and 71.9% of jobs did not start within five minutes. These figures show the potential scale of CI disruption, though the excerpt gives no cause or remediation.

item.title: Kubernetes node swap raises workload density by up to 3× with little latency cost
item.description: Benchmarks across kernel builds, headless browsers and isolated Python runtimes found up to 3× higher node density using swap backed by NVMe, often with little or no latency cost. This offers a concrete way to stretch memory-bound clusters running bursty or agent workloads.

item.title: UCEPROTECT ASN-wide listings can block innocent DigitalOcean sites
item.description: The account says UCEPROTECT Level 3 lists whole ASNs, causing Orange filters to block sites, and offers whitelisting for a monthly fee. It shows how reputation lists can create reachability problems beyond the individual server.

item.title: Rootless Podman exposes a Docker-compatible socket for docker-compose
item.description: The guide shows how to use Podman's user-level UNIX socket with Docker ecosystem tools, including docker-compose, and explains the user-namespace mapping. This is a practical option for running familiar container workflows without root access.

item.title: OpenSSH reverse forwarding and Nginx provide self-hosted HTTP tunnels
item.description: The guide combines SSH remote forwarding on an automatically allocated port with an Nginx wildcard host that proxies requests to the forwarded service. It offers a practical self-hosted alternative for exposing local previews without a dedicated tunnel client.

item.title: Custom-domain email separates simple forwarding from sending
item.description: Cloudflare Email Routing can forward incoming mail, but the excerpt says sending is the problem; the author compares hosted and self-managed options. The trade-offs are useful for engineers choosing low-cost email infrastructure.

item.title: Cloudflare is opening more Enterprise-only features to all customers
item.description: Cloudflare says it is making capabilities previously limited to Enterprise customers available across its customer base. Broader access could change the options available to teams building on its platform, though the excerpt names no specific features.

item.title: gVisor’s CNCF donation shifts the project to foundation governance
item.description: Google’s donation of gVisor, including its name and trademarks, was accepted by CNCF, changing the project’s governance model. Teams relying on this container isolation layer should watch how its stewardship develops.

item.title: Cloudflare unifies logs, traces, analytics, and alerts in one platform
item.description: The updates include end-to-end edge-to-origin tracing, a unified SQL query API, custom alerts, and data export. The platform-wide view could simplify diagnosis across services, although the excerpt gives no performance or architecture details.

item.title: Cloudflare is fastest across 74% of the 1,000 largest networks
item.description: Cloudflare reports a rise from 60% to 74% since April, using a new measurement methodology that includes Challenge Pages. The results and measurement approach offer a view into how a large network tracks performance across providers.

item.title: Oracle deployment on Amazon EVS uses FSx for ONTAP NFS datastores
item.description: The walkthrough covers provisioning storage, mounting NFS datastores, installing Oracle 19c, and configuring SnapMirror replication. It offers practical deployment steps for teams running Oracle on VMware in AWS.

item.title: Deploy AWS regional-availability data inside your VPC
item.description: The post describes deploying AWS service-availability data as infrastructure teams control, with refresh schedules and workload-specific filtering. That can help multi-Region teams automate availability checks within their own network and governance.
